title: Compatible coefficient maps give a linear strict tensor tower
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe and let $R,S,B_n$ ($n\geq1$) be sheaves of commutative rings. Let $r_n:R\to B_n$, $p_n:S\to B_n$ and $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ satisfy $b_nr_{n+1}=r_n$ and $b_np_{n+1}=p_n$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system] and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an $R$-module $M$ set $V_n(M)=\operatorname{Res}_{p_n}(M\otimes_R B_n)$, with transition $x\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes b_n(z)$. These maps exist uniquely with the displayed formula on the images of presheaf pure tensors and define an additive functor $V:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(S))$ sending $f$ to $(f\otimes1)_n$. On complexes the transitions commute with the termwise integer-shift comparisons. Its termwise cochain functor preserves homotopies and has coherent integer-shift comparisons. Restriction along each $p_n$ preserves and reflects quasi-isomorphisms. If $k$ is a commutative ring with compatible homomorphisms to the rings of global sections of $R,S$ whose composites into every $B_n$ agree, the induced scalar actions make $V$ $k$-linear [def-weil-linear-category, def-weil-linear-functor].

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), presheaf tensor, sheafification and bilinear universal property; termwise homotopies and shifts use homology.tex, definition-shift-cochain. Agent-written strict tower refinement.

proof.text:
For each object $U$ put $P_n(M)(U)=M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}B_n(U)$, with $B_n(U)$ acting on the second factor. For $a\in R(U)$ the proposed transition respects balancing because
$$ax\otimes b_n(z)=x\otimes r_n(a)b_n(z)=x\otimes b_n(r_{n+1}(a)z).$$
It respects addition in both variables. Thus $q_n(x\otimes z)=x\otimes b_n(z)$ is an additive map of tensors. Give $P_n(M)$ the $S$-action $s(x\otimes z)=x\otimes p_n(s)z$. Then
$$q_n(x\otimes p_{n+1}(s)z)=x\otimes p_n(s)b_n(z)=s q_n(x\otimes z).$$
The maps commute with restriction along every arrow of the site because $b_n,r_n,p_n$ are maps of ring sheaves and the tensor restrictions send $x\otimes z$ to $x|\otimes z|$. Hence $q_n$ is a morphism of presheaves of $S$-modules. These are ordinary tensor generators and relations checks, using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), presheaf tensor construction; explicit compatible-coefficient calculation

proof.text: Sheafify $P_n(M)$ as a presheaf of $B_n$-modules. Its sheafification is $M\otimes_R B_n$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] the underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of $P_n(M)$. If instead $P_n(M)$ is sheafified as an $S$-module, its underlying abelian sheaf is the same one. The $S$-action obtained from $p_n$ on $M\otimes_R B_n$ extends the original action on $P_n(M)$, so it equals the sheafified $S$-action by the uniqueness of action extension in that lemma. Consequently this $S$-module sheafification is canonically $V_n(M)$. Apply the lemma's unique factorization to $P_{n+1}(M)\xrightarrow{q_n}P_n(M)\to V_n(M)$, obtaining $t_n:V_{n+1}(M)\to V_n(M)$. Additive maps out of the abelian sheafification are determined by their composites with its unit, by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. On a presheaf tensor, an additive map is determined by pure tensors. Therefore $t_n$ is the unique $S$-linear sheaf map with the formula in the statement. This does not assume that arbitrary sheaf sections are global pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), underlying abelian sheafification, uniqueness of the module action and factorization; Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: For an $R$-linear sheaf map $f:M\to N$, the maps $P_n(M)\to P_n(N)$ given by $x\otimes z\mapsto f(x)\otimes z$ respect balancing, restrictions and the $S$-action. Their unique sheafified maps $V_n(f)$ exist by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The two composites $t_n(N)V_{n+1}(f)$ and $V_n(f)t_n(M)$ send $x\otimes z$ to $f(x)\otimes b_n(z)$, hence agree by step 2's uniqueness. Identity and composition likewise send a generator to $x\otimes z$ and $g(f(x))\otimes z$. Finally $(f+g)(x)\otimes z=f(x)\otimes z+g(x)\otimes z$ and $0(x)\otimes z=0$; uniqueness gives $V_n(f+g)=V_n(f)+V_n(g)$ and $V_n(0)=0$.

Take $(V_n(M),t_n(M))_{n\geq1}$ as a tower in the sense of [def-weil-inverse-system]. The commuting squares of step 3 make $(V_n(f))_n$ a morphism of towers, and identities, compositions and sums are componentwise. For $m>n$ the map is the composite $t_n\cdots t_{m-1}$; associativity supplies all tower functor identities, without an additional coherence choice. Zero objects and biproducts in the tower category are the componentwise ones, with transitions the corresponding zero or block diagonal maps; their universal properties follow componentwise. Since the functor preserves zero maps and addition by step 3, it sends the biproduct equations $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\iota_1\pi_1+\iota_2\pi_2=1$ to the same equations. Thus $V$ is an additive functor to the strict tower category.

source.place: Agent strict-tower refinement of Tag 03EK: adjacent transitions and componentwise morphisms

proof.text:
For a cochain complex $K$, apply $V$ to each $K^i$ and to $d_K^i$. The relation $d^{i+1}d^i=0$ remains true since $V$ preserves composition and zero. Each transition is a cochain map because step 3 applied to $f=d_K^i$ gives $t_n^{i+1}V_{n+1}(d_K^i)=V_n(d_K^i)t_n^i$. The same equation for any cochain map gives the termwise cochain functor. If $h^i:K^i\to L^{i-1}$ is a homotopy from $f$ to $g$, its equation is $f^i-g^i=d_L^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_K^i$. Applying the additive functor gives
$$V(f^i)-V(g^i)=V(d_L^{i-1})V(h^i)+V(h^{i+1})V(d_K^i),$$
so $(V(h^i))_i$ is the required homotopy in towers. Its components are tower morphisms by step 3.

source.place: Section complexes, cochain homotopy equation immediately before lemma-compose-homotopy-cochain; direct additive calculation

proof.text: Use $(K[a])^i=K^{i+a}$ and $d_{K[a]}^i=(-1)^a d_K^{i+a}$ for $a\in\mathbf Z$. The comparison $V(K[a])\to V(K)[a]$ is the identity on each object $V(K^{i+a})$. It is a cochain map because additivity gives $V((-1)^a d)=(-1)^a V(d)$, including negative integers $a$. Naturality in $K$ is the identity on the components $V(f^{i+a})$. At level $n$, the square with the transition and the two shift comparisons has $t_n(K^{i+a})$ on both paths, so the level comparisons form a comparison of towers. The comparison for zero is the identity. For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, both the direct comparison for $a+b$ and the composite comparisons have the identity on $V(K^{i+a+b})$ after the canonical reindexing; their differentials agree since $(-1)^{a+b}=(-1)^a(-1)^b$. This proves the unit and addition coherence for all integer shifts.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and write $U_{B_n}$ and $U_S$ for the forgetful functors from module sheaves to abelian sheaves. The site is small in the module universe, so abelian sheafification exists and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], clause (1), applies to both ring sheaves. Both forgetful functors preserve kernels and cokernels, and $U_S\operatorname{Res}_{p_n}=U_{B_n}$ by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. It follows by the formula $H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ that the underlying abelian sheaves of $H^i(\operatorname{Res}_{p_n}K)$ and $H^i(K)$ are canonically the same, naturally in the complex $K$. Explicitly images are kernels of cokernels, so the same underlying kernel, image and quotient are used on both sides.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian): kernels, cokernels and exactness correspond to those of underlying abelian sheaves

proof.text: A module-sheaf map whose underlying abelian-sheaf map is invertible has a module-linear inverse: if $u$ is module-linear and $v=u^{-1}$, then $u(v(a y))=a y=u(a v(y))$, and injectivity of $u$ gives $v(a y)=a v(y)$ on every object. Thus both forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms. By step 7, a cochain map of $B_n$-modules induces isomorphisms on cohomology exactly when its restriction along $p_n$ does. This proves preservation and reflection of quasi-isomorphisms using their definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No exactness assertion about the tensor functor itself is needed.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), and direct linearity check for the inverse of an underlying abelian-sheaf isomorphism

proof.text:
For $a\in k$ write $a_R,a_S$ for its global sections, and $a_n$ for their common image in $B_n$. Restrictions of these global sections act on every local section. On module-sheaf Hom groups define $(af)(x)=a_R f(x)$, or $a_S f(x)$ on the target. These are module maps since the coefficient rings are commutative; addition and the module axioms hold on sections, and composition is $k$-bilinear. On tower morphisms take this action componentwise: it preserves the transition squares because transitions are $S$-linear. This gives the $k$-linear category structures of [def-weil-linear-category]. On presheaf pure tensors,
$$V_n(af)(x\otimes z)=a_R f(x)\otimes z=f(x)\otimes a_n z=a_S\bigl(f(x)\otimes z\bigr).$$
By step 2's uniqueness the sheaf maps satisfy $V_n(af)=aV_n(f)$ at every level. Together with additivity, this is exactly the $k$-linear-functor condition [def-weil-linear-functor].

Step 9: k-linearity needs r_n(a_R)=p_n(a_S), which is exactly the hypothesis. Small cases tested: one-object site, zero objects, identity tower, ℤ→ℤ/2^n, nonflat B_n.
